_comment: GENERATED by scripts/build-calibration.mjs. What each null-tested method on the site reports on data where the null is true by construction, beside what it reports on the real text.

tests.nullDescription: 100 copies of the text with the words shuffled inside every verse
tests.realFindings: 1003 of 1669 candidates pass BH at q <= 0.05
tests.nullFindings: 0.06 pass on average (at most 1); 6 of 100 copies have any
tests.reading: The share of null copies with any finding estimates how often the whole analysis would report something in noise; Benjamini-Hochberg aims to keep it near 0.05.

tests.nullFindings: 0.03 pass on average (at most 2); 2 of 100 copies have any
tests.reading: The share of null copies with any finding estimates how often the whole analysis would report something in noise; Benjamini-Hochberg aims to keep it near 0.05.

tests.nullFindings: 0.13 pass on average (at most 2); 12 of 100 copies have any
tests.reading: The share of null copies with any finding estimates how often the whole analysis would report something in noise; Benjamini-Hochberg aims to keep it near 0.05.

tests.method: Period keyness (G2 against a surah-to-period permutation null)
tests.nullDescription: 40 random relabelings of the surahs, each tested against its own fresh permutations
tests.realFindings: 132 of 6568 root-period tests pass BH at q <= 0.05
tests.nullFindings: 1.35 pass on average (at most 54); 1 of 40 relabelings have any
tests.reading: Findings arrive in bursts (several roots at once) because roots share surahs; the share of relabelings with any finding is the figure to compare with 0.05.

tests.method: Surah distance (permutation null, BH over 6,441 pairs)
tests.nullDescription: 10 texts in which all 6,236 verses are shuffled across the whole Qur'an and cut into pseudo-surahs of the real surahs' verse counts; the full pairwise pipeline at 200 draws per pair
tests.realFindings: 5248 of 6441 pairs pass BH at q <= 0.05
tests.nullFindings: 0 pairs pass on average (at most 0); 4.93% of pairs have p <= 0.05; mean excess -0.0004
tests.reading: On a text where verse order carries no surah structure the share of raw p <= 0.05 should be near 5% and the mean excess near 0. This checks the code and the BH step; it says nothing about whether real surahs are exchangeable collections of verses, which they are not, and that is the finding.

tests.method: Period heterogeneity of root-pair association (Cochran Q)
tests.nullDescription: 5 assignments of a random period to every verse, period sizes kept; the same pipeline
tests.realFindings: 14 of 5203 pairs pass BH at q <= 0.05
tests.nullFindings: 1% of pairs have raw p <= 0.05 (nominal 5%); 0 pass BH on average
tests.reading: A raw rate well below 0.05 means the test is conservative: with sparse counts in the smaller periods the chi-square reference over-states the variance of the estimates, so the pairs that pass are real but many period-specific pairs will be missed. The count of significant pairs is a lower bound.
